reading.body:
TierPoint Little Rock publishes 9,000 square feet of technical space and no IT load figure in megawatts. Without a published power number, no translation into rack count or accelerator capacity is possible from the data this site holds. The footprint is small by hyperscale standards, and the absence of a power figure means the campus cannot be ranked against AI infrastructure by the metric that matters most to scaling decisions.

The six certifications tell a specific story about what this facility is qualified to host. SOC 1 Type 2 and ISO 27001 establish audited controls over financial reporting processes and information security management. PCI DSS qualifies it for payment card data environments. HIPAA and HITRUST together qualify it for protected health information workloads, with HITRUST adding a third-party validated control framework on top of the regulatory baseline. ITAR qualifies it for controlled defense-related technical data. None of those certifications speaks to the high-density power infrastructure that AI training workloads require.

Arkansas has two facilities mapped in this site's data, and neither publishes a megawatt figure, so the state total stands at zero published MW. TierPoint Little Rock ranks first in the state by published MW only because no facility in the state publishes any. That ranking carries no practical meaning for capacity comparison. For a reader deciding whether this campus matters to AI, the honest answer from the available data is that it is a compliance-oriented colocation facility of modest size, and nothing published here positions it as an AI training or large-scale inference site.
